messages:
sara (infra): Heads up — staging GPU cluster in us-west-2 showing ~15% nodes NotReady after last network-policy rollout. seeing 'kubelet: dial tcp 10.0.45.23:10250: i/o timeout' in syslog on several nodes. anyone touching NACLs or KMS recently?

mike (oncall): Not me. grabbing logs. 

ops-bot: Deploybot: network-policy/staging-gpu rolled at 2026-09-18T14:07:02Z by mike (oncall) — rollout complete.

sara (infra): hmm ops-bot shows network-policy change, but timing matches. also noticed bootstrap script failing to decrypt /etc/gpu-secrets with KMS error on 4 nodes: "AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt"

linh (security): :thinking_face: KMS policy was tightened yesterday to remove cross-account roles from decrypt by default. did we onboard the gpu-provisioner role into the new key policy?

alex (sre): quick check: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady` shows 7 nodes NotReady. healthcheck probe uses ephemeral ports 30000-32767 for node-probe -> could be NACL blocking ephemeral outbound. NACL change would explain kubelet timeout and failed bootstrap if they can't reach kms via NAT.

mike (oncall): digging VPC flow logs. `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a1b2c3d` shows a deny rule added at 14:06 that blocks ephemeral ports. suspect the network-policy rollout pipeline also applied a protective NACL change (mis-scoped).

sara (infra): oh — the rollout automation has two steps: network-policy + emergency NACL harden when flag `secure-subnet=true`. Looks like flag was accidentally set for the staging GPU subnet.

linh (security): action: KMS key policy still needs the gpu-provisioner role. but we should treat this as two independent failures: (1) NACL blocked ephemeral -> kubelet timeouts & health failures; (2) KMS policy prevents decrypt when nodes attempt to finish bootstrapping. both needed to bring nodes fully ready.

alex (sre): immediate mitigation: rollback the NACL deny rule and re-run node bootstrap on affected instances. I'm applying a temporary permissive NACL for the subnet and asking provisioner to re-encrypt secrets if needed.

mike (oncall): applied revert at 14:20 UTC — NACL rule removed. nodes are re-attempting kubelet connection. flowlogs show traffic to 3.80.12.45:443 (KMS endpoint) failing earlier, now allowed.

ops-bot: Instance manager: restarted kubelet on i-0c12345, i-0d67890, i-0f24680 as part of remediation.

sara (infra): after restart, 6/7 nodes came back to Ready within 2m. one node still failing with KMS AccessDenied.

linh (security): I'll patch the KMS key policy now to explicitly allow arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gpu-provisioner and the staging account role `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/staging-bootstrap`. Will add the minimal principal and kms:Decrypt permission.

alex (sre): while lin patching, I'll run `ssh i-0f24680 'journalctl -u kubelet -n 200'` and `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://encrypted_secret` to confirm.

linh (security): KMS policy updated at 14:42 UTC. policy change id: key-policy-20260918-staging-fix. added principals and limited to decrypt for alias/aws/redwood/staging-gpu.

mike (oncall): re-run bootstrap on i-0f24680 -> decrypt succeeded. node joined at 14:49 UTC. all 7 nodes Ready.

sara (infra): good recovery. root cause summary for now: automation flag mis-set triggered NACL harden for staging GPU subnet, blocking ephemeral ports and outbound to KMS; separately, tightened KMS key policy lacked the staging provisioner role which prevented decrypt during bootstrap. both combined caused the healthcheck cascade.

compliance-bot: Noted: security change and network automation interaction affected staging. Filing ticket COMP-2026-348 for audit and postmortem. Please include change IDs and timeline.

linh (security): follow-ups: 1) add a canary gate in rollout pipeline that prevents NACL harden in staging unless `allow-harden` approved; 2) update KMS onboarding checklist to include gpu-provisioner and subnet bootstrap roles; 3) run a cross-check between infra automation flags and subnet tags to avoid mis-scoping.

alex (sre): I'll add a runbook section: 'Staging GPU node NotReady due to NACL/KMS' with quick commands to check and revert NACL and patch KMS.

mike (oncall): cost note: while investigating we saw ~120GB cross-AZ egress because some pods re-scheduled across AZs during the outage. filing cost-ops FYI.

sara (infra): Thanks everyone. I'll open the postmortem draft and link COMP-2026-348. please add any logs/change ids you have. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Ticket created: COMP-2026-348. Postmortem draft: https://redwood.internal/pm/COMP-2026-348

mike (oncall): marking thread resolved. will follow up in the postmortem with timeline and remediation tasks.

sara (infra): resolved — nodes healthy. planning a rehearse of the rollout pipeline in a sandbox next week to catch misflags.
